scenarios.prompt: Write a TypeScript function that looks up a user by ID from a Map<string, User>. Handle the case where the user doesn't exist. Do not return null or undefined.
criteria: Uses Option.from(), Option.some(), or Option.none() (or the equivalent some()/none()/toOption() functions) instead of null/undefined
Does not return null or undefined directly from the function
Uses .match() or .orElse() to handle the absent case at the call site

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: given a user ID, get the user from a cache (Map<string, User>), then get their profile (Map<string, Profile>), then get their avatar URL (profile.avatarUrl may be undefined). Each step may return nothing. Chain these safely without nested null checks.
criteria: Uses .bind() or .bindAsync() to chain optional steps (.map() is also acceptable for reading a field that may be undefined, since map turns null/undefined into none)
Does not use nested if/null checks between steps
The chain stops at the first absent value without explicit branching

scenarios.prompt: Express + Redis + Prisma app. Write an async function that gets a session token from Redis (returns string | null), validates it to get a user ID (async, may return null), then loads the user from Prisma (may return null). Return a 404 response if any step returns nothing.
criteria: Uses Option for absent values instead of null checks
Uses Option.fromAsync() and/or .bindAsync() for the async optional steps
Produces the 404/success response with .match() or .orElse() on the async Option chain (these return a Promise there), or with .matchAsync()/.orElseAsync()

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: resolve a user's UI theme. Read it from userSettings (Map<string, string>, keyed by user ID); the stored value may be missing or may be an unsupported string, and only 'light', 'dark' and 'system' are valid. When the user has no valid theme, write a debug log line, then fall back to the organization default from orgSettings (Map<string, string>, same rules: may be missing or invalid). If that also yields nothing, use 'system'. Write it as one chain, without if statements or null checks.
criteria: Drops a theme that is not one of the supported values with .filter() on the Option or with the noneWhen predicate of Option.from(value, noneWhen) (instead of an if or a ternary)
Falls back to the organization default with .bindNone() or .mapNone() on the Option chain (not with nested null checks or by unwrapping the first Option)
Logs the debug line with .onNone() (or .onSome() for the found case) inside the chain, and still ends with .orElse('system') or .match() to produce the final string

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: get a product by SKU. First look in an in-memory cache (Map<string, Product>); if it is not there, load it from the database with db.findProduct(sku): Promise<Product | null>. Write a debug log whenever a product is found. Return an async result that is either a NotFoundError (which must include the SKU) or the Product, so the HTTP layer can turn it into a 404.
criteria: Falls back to the async database load with .bindNoneAsync() or .mapNoneAsync() on the cache Option, instead of an if/else on the cache result
Converts the Option (or OptionAsync) into an Either with its .toEither(...) method, passing a NotFoundError value or factory that includes the SKU
Logs found products with .onSome() in the chain, not with a separate isSome() check or an if

scenarios.prompt: NestJS + TypeORM service. Load a customer's loyalty points from the repository (findPoints(customerId): number | undefined). Map the points to a tier: 10000 or more is 'gold', 5000 or more is 'silver', anything else is 'bronze'. Then pick a coupon for the tier: gold customers get a personal coupon from couponService.personal(customerId): Promise<Coupon>, silver and bronze customers get couponService.standard(tier): Promise<Coupon>. A customer without points gets no coupon. Avoid if/else ladders and nested ternaries; the method returns the coupon as an optional value.
criteria: Uses .guardMap() with [when, then] guard pairs (and an otherwise function) to map the points to a tier, instead of if/else or a chain of ternaries
Uses .guardMapAsync() or .guardBindAsync() to choose between the personal and the standard coupon call
Returns an Option/OptionAsync (or a Promise of an Option) for the coupon, never null/undefined, and an absent customer skips the tier and coupon steps
